title: The Deep Cover
premise: Jonah Underhill, a burnt-out financial-crimes investigator, receives calls on a burner phone from Mara Voss — the undercover informant who vanished twelve years ago and whom he loved and lost to protocol. Her voice pulls him into a conspiracy inside his own agency: a laundering network is staging a catastrophic 'accident' at a coastal refinery to bury evidence of a decade of dirty money. As Jonah goes off-book with a ragtag team of exiles — a disgraced analyst, a retired port inspector, and Mara herself, alive but changed — he must choose between the rules that defined him and the justice they've failed to deliver. The novel ends with Jonah exposing the network by feeding its own laundered ledger to the public, saving the refinery at terrible personal cost, and walking away from the agency with Mara, finally free of both duty and cover.
about_author: Wendell Almeida is a former compliance auditor who spent nine years tracing shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction full-time. He writes from a small harbor town where he claims half his neighbors are former informants, though none will confirm it.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Twelve years into investigating financial crimes that never stick, Jonah audits another sanitized ledger and feels the hollowness of a career built on paperwork. Emotional beat: quiet despair disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Burner That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A package arrives with no sender: a burner phone that rings once. He answers against every instinct, hears breathing, then a click. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Her Voice
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The phone rings again; the voice is Mara Voss, the informant declared dead twelve years ago, the woman he loved and reported on. She says only: 'They're going to make it look like an accident.' Emotional beat: vertigo, grief reopened.

chapters.title: Protocol Says Hang Up
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah reports the contact to his supervisor, Deputy Director Hale, who orders him to surrender the phone. He pockets it instead. Emotional beat: first conscious betrayal of the rules.

chapters.title: What Drowned in Graywater
chapters.summary: POV Mara, twelve years earlier. Flashback: Mara's recruitment as an undercover asset inside the Caldera shipping syndicate, and her growing bond with her handler, Jonah. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by deception.

chapters.title: The Refinery at Point Alder
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Following Mara's cryptic coordinates, Jonah surveils the Point Alder refinery and finds security contracts funneled through shells he recognizes from old cases. Emotional beat: dread clicking into pattern.

chapters.title: Dead Files Walking
chapters.summary: POV Odile Ferran, disgraced analyst. Odile, fired for flagging the same shells years ago, is visited by Jonah. She agrees to help, mostly out of spite. Emotional beat: bitter kinship between two people the system discarded.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Mara, present day. Mara watches Jonah from a distance, wrestling with whether using him makes her a handler or a monster. Emotional beat: guilt braided with longing.

chapters.title: Hale's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah probes Hale's travel records and finds unexplained meetings with Caldera-linked lawyers. His own agency may be inside the loop. Emotional beat: the floor giving way beneath his identity.

chapters.title: The Port Inspector's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Reyes, retired port inspector. Reyes kept private manifests for thirty years out of stubbornness; now Jonah needs them. Emotional beat: found family beginning — three strangers choosing each other.

chapters.title: Accident, Scheduled
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The manifests reveal a shipment of industrial catalyst mislabeled as lubricant, timed to arrive at Point Alder in nineteen days. An explosion would vaporize the evidence warehouse beside it. Emotional beat: cold clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: Meeting the Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In a rain-soaked parking structure, Jonah finally meets Mara face to face after twelve years. Neither trusts the other; both want to. Emotional beat: love and suspicion in the same breath.

chapters.title: Cover Stories
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara explains how she survived: the syndicate faked her death to protect a bigger asset, and she's been running her own counter-operation since. Emotional beat: the cost of a life lived as a lie.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile notices surveillance on their safehouse — someone inside the group may be leaking. Paranoia takes root. Emotional beat: trust fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The team maps the attack window and realizes the agency's official investigation is being steered away from Point Alder — by Hale. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Everything
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. Reyes identifies the signatory linking Caldera to the refinery contract: a mid-level fixer named Bram Ostergaard, invisible until you know his name. Emotional beat: small victories, large stakes.

chapters.title: Ostergaard's Price
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah corners Ostergaard with leverage from the old cases; the fixer offers information in exchange for extraction. Emotional beat: moral compromise tasting like necessity.

chapters.title: What Mara Buried
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Flashback: the night of her 'death,' when she chose to disappear rather than blow Jonah's career — and let him believe she betrayed him. Emotional beat: heartbreak reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The safehouse is raided; the team scatters. Someone gave them up. Odile suspects Reyes; Jonah refuses to believe it. Emotional beat: the found family tested by fire.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Suspended and stripped of credentials, Jonah learns Hale has flagged him as a rogue element — the perfect scapegoat if the refinery burns. Emotional beat: hunted by the institution he served.

chapters.title: The Middle of It
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara reveals the deeper truth: the 'attack' isn't just destruction — it's a reset, wiping a decade of transactions so the network can restart clean. Emotional beat: scale of the horror sinking in.

chapters.title: Reyes's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. Cornered, Reyes admits he was approached years ago and took one payment — but never leaked. His shame nearly breaks the team before Odile finds the real leak's digital fingerprint. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of faith.

chapters.title: The Real Leak
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The fingerprint traces to a junior analyst in Hale's office — a true believer being used as an unwitting conduit. They decide to turn her rather than burn her. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. With the turned analyst's access, the team confirms the catalyst shipment's route and a second, human target: a whistleblower scheduled to be 'on site' during the accident. Emotional beat: urgency sharpened by conscience.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara extracts Ostergaard from a syndicate safehouse in a tense night drive, proving her loyalty to the team with blood and risk. Emotional beat: trust earned in motion.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. They reach the whistleblower, Elena Sart, a refinery safety officer who suspected the sabotage and was told to stay silent. She joins them. Emotional beat: courage is contagious.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Hale privately offers Jonah reinstatement and Mara's head in exchange for walking away. Jonah understands he was never meant to survive this either way. Emotional beat: the choice made plain.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara tells Jonah to take the deal and save himself; he refuses. For the first time, they speak plainly about what they were to each other. Emotional beat: love chosen over survival.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The team finalizes the plan: intercept the catalyst, seize the master ledger during the chaos, and broadcast it before Hale can spin the aftermath. Emotional beat: terrified determination.

chapters.title: Dry Run
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. A rehearsal at the port goes wrong when syndicate scouts spot them; Reyes covers the retreat and is injured. Emotional beat: sacrifice binding the family tighter.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Quiet chapter: the team shares a last meal, stories, fears. Jonah and Mara stand watch together and almost speak of a future. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: Point Alder, Day One
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The operation begins: Mara infiltrates the refinery as a contractor while Jonah and Odile position at the manifest office. Emotional beat: controlled terror.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The catalyst truck is diverted and hidden; but the syndicate's backup plan activates early — the alarm sequence starts ahead of schedule. Emotional beat: the plan unraveling.

chapters.title: Hale's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Confronting Hale in the emergency operations center, Jonah forces him to choose between triggering the 'accident' and preserving deniability. Hale hesitates — and that hesitation costs him. Emotional beat: the corrupt exposed in real time.

chapters.title: Firewall
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile fights a clock-side battle in the server room, copying the master ledger while syndicate technicians try to wipe it. Emotional beat: one woman versus a machine of money.

chapters.title: The Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara disables the ignition chain manually, nearly dying in the process, as the refinery stands down in confusion. Emotional beat: triumph laced with grief for what it cost.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The ledger goes public — every shell, every signature, including Hale's. Arrests begin before dawn. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, delivered anyway.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. Recovering, Reyes watches the news coverage with the team scattered around his kitchen. Elena testifies; Ostergaard disappears into witness protection. Emotional beat: exhausted, imperfect peace.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah declines reinstatement, hands over his badge, and walks out of the agency that rewrote its rules one time too many. Emotional beat: liberation in relinquishment.

chapters.title: No Cover Required
chapters.summary: POV Mara and Jonah. On the harbor road out of town, two burner phones go into the sea. No aliases, no handlers, no mission — just two people and an open road. Emotional beat: love, finally uncovered.
